conventions.convention: Time series are real processes indexed by Z. Strict stationarity preserves every finite-dimensional law under every integer shift and imposes no moments. Weak stationarity requires finite second moments, constant mean, and lag-only covariance.

The population ACVF is γ(h)=Cov(X(t+h),X(t)). Samples start at t=1 and have length n≥1. Both sample ACVFs use sample-mean centering, absolute lag, and zero extension at |h|≥n; their denominators are respectively n and n−|h|. Neither name asserts unbiasedness.
The ergodic mean result assumes AC and integrability, and uses ergodicity of the canonical one-sided path shift for Y(k)=X(k+1), k≥0.

load_bearing.statement: Strict stationarity means invariance of all finite-dimensional laws under every common integer shift. Weak stationarity means finite second moments, a time-independent mean, and covariance γ(h)=Cov(X(t+h),X(t)) independent of t.

For real data of length n≥1, the biased sample ACVF is the sample-mean-centered lag-product sum divided by n for |h|<n and zero otherwise. The pair-count-normalized rescaling instead divides by n−|h| on that same domain and is zero otherwise.

For a weakly stationary real process, Var(X̄_n)=n⁻²∑_{|h|<n}(n−|h|)γ(h). Absolute covariance summability gives 0≤Var(X̄_n)≤n⁻¹∑_{h∈Z}|γ(h)| and L² consistency for the mean. Every finite real data vector has a zero-extended biased sample ACVF with nonnegative Toeplitz quadratic forms.

alerts.finding: Proof 1.1 defines g* as the pointwise limit on the convergence set and zero elsewhere. Proof 2.1 then says: “For ε>0, every point of D_{m,k} belongs to the positive-maximal set of (g−(k/m−ε))1_{D_{m,k}}.” The universal pointwise assertion need not hold on the exceptional null set assigned g*=0. For example, take X={p} disjoint union {1,2,...}, give p probability one and every integer probability zero, set T(p)=p, T(j)=j+1, g(p)=0 and g(j)=−j². This is a finite measure-preserving system with integrable finite-valued g. The averages diverge to −∞ on every integer, so the prescribed g* is zero everywhere and D_{m,0}=X. With ε=1/2, every partial sum of g+ε starting at an integer is negative, so those points are outside the positive-maximal set. The missing qualification concerns only a null set and does not undermine the integral conclusion.

seams_checked.note: The observed finite coordinate record, pushforward law, joint-law conditioning, and application-specific scientific fields agree with the contract. The page correctly separates mathematical consequences from empirical adequacy.

The spectral definition and theorem facts preserve real weak stationarity, finite second moments, and γ(h)=Cov(X(t+h),X(t)). The known-mean periodogram explicitly distinguishes its centering from sample-mean centering.

The ARMA definition and consumer facts preserve the weak-stationarity interface. White noise is explicitly uncorrelated rather than assumed independent; inference claims retain their separate strict-stationarity, ergodicity, and iid hypotheses.

Forecast definitions, normal equations, and recursion use square-integrability and the stated lag convention faithfully. Nonsingularity and positive definiteness are additional consumer hypotheses, rather than consequences attributed to stationarity.
The page and general kernel definition cite stationarity only to explain that finite-horizon state-space laws do not require it; no stationary mean or lag-covariance conclusion is inferred.

Spatial strict stationarity is explicitly an extension to admissible common translations. Wide stationarity retains finite second moments, constant mean, and displacement-only covariance. Intrinsic increment stationarity is separately defined.
